title: Entrance Fee Agreement: One Agreement per Resident and the Paired Residency
content:
A customer holds at most **1** Entrance Fee Agreement at a time. A couple sharing an apartment holds one agreement with double occupancy and the second person entrance fee of the plan, never two agreements.

## The signing condition

A new Entrance Fee Agreement may be signed only when the customer has no other agreement in reserved, occupied, terminated or refund scheduled status. The condition is read from the agreements on record under that customer, not from what the caller says about them.

| Status of an existing agreement held by the customer | Effect on signing a new agreement under this rule |
|---|---|
| Reserved | A new agreement may not be signed |
| Occupied | A new agreement may not be signed |
| Terminated | A new agreement may not be signed |
| Refund scheduled | A new agreement may not be signed |
| Closed, rescinded or cancelled | Does not stand in the way under this rule |

## Pairing with the independent living residency

An Entrance Fee Agreement is always paired with the Larkspur independent living residency for the same apartment: the agreement names that residency. The independent living monthly fee of an entrance fee resident follows the monthly fee adjustment of the refund plan, applied under the terms of the Independent Living Residency Agreement.

## Points of judgement

- Two spouses moving into one apartment: one agreement, double occupancy, with the second person entrance fee.
- A resident whose earlier agreement is still awaiting its refund (terminated or refund scheduled) does not sign a second agreement while that one stands in either status.
